angle: A scientific instrument. The chart is the page: one log ruler from 15 to 1,000, drawn like a slide rule. Every build is a range bar with its own silhouette hanging off that ruler. Uncertainty and status are always drawn, never left to footnotes: bars are ranges, hatching means "assumed", empty stretches are hatched voids, and the extrapolation boundary is a red rule.
summary:
The mockup is a single page in the Build Calculator's type system (Big Shoulders Display, Public Sans, IBM Plex Mono) and its status-chip vocabulary. The page is a stack of plates, the way an instrument is a stack of panels:
1. Masthead: one verdict sentence carrying the four anchor numbers (20 to 26, 38, 160 and 180, 924).
2. "The scale" plate, which is the hero. A widened template man (ANSUR II proportions, grey, dotted, labelled NOT A BUILD) stands at 24, 48, 96, 192 and 384, then the meatball circle at 924. The T/A/F functional-limit brackets sit between those figures and the ruler. The ivory slide-rule ruler carries dense log ticks. Its bottom edge is a conversion scale: the same reading as kg of fat-free mass for a 1.80 m man (S × 3.24). Below the ruler are six group lanes: every build is a thin range plus a tick at its working value. Hatched voids run through the lanes wherever no build's range reaches. Further marks: the Kouri 25 hairline, the frame-based prediction bracket, a red "measured humans end, extrapolation beyond" rule, and a shaded "past 924: impossible" end. The plate also holds the key (outline marking, bar anatomy, status chips).
3. "The ranking" plate: a forest plot of all 49 builds, lowest to highest. Each row has a silhouette (same height, skull-top datum line), name, the build's height, weight and fat range each boxed in its status border, a bar on the shared log track, the score range, plain FFMI and status chips. Gap rows such as "Nothing from 42 to 57 · Empty until Step 2" are inserted in sequence. The list closes with the meatball row, then Wolverine as "not scored". The axis is sticky. Controls: figure size, scale zoom, view, group filters. Clicking a name expands a detail panel (inputs with sources, each girth and which outline it produced, what the model ignores).
4. "How the score works": a formula block and a worked table (Army median, Coleman, Rex: plain FFMI against score).
5. "Measuring bench": the sample sheet (Rex's traced turnaround) with guide lines carried across the views, the tail painted out, and width/depth slice markers. Beside it: inputs, a checks list (PASS/CHECK/FAIL chips with numbers), a results table with ± columns, a Copy button and the duo.jpg validation line. Below: "Target outline" with front and side black-on-white outline images at the sheet spec.
6. "Known limits", in short bullet form.

Rex and Ollie are real traces from the turnarounds. My mock-grade tracer uses a saturation/dark/warm mask, hole fill, Moore boundary tracing and Ramer-Douglas-Peucker simplification. The tails are split off with hand-placed polygons, and the skull-top lines are eyeballed. Human figures are generated from outline.json fractions: skeletal joints stay fixed, and part widths scale by each part's girth÷height against ANSUR, or by mass when the girth is unknown. All numbers are mock, but built from builds.json heights, weights and girths with made-up body-fat ranges. Checks pass at 390 and 1280 in light and dark: no horizontal scroll, no NaN, undefined or Infinity, no console errors. That includes the option modes (zoom, real heights, side view).

styles.figure_treatment: Flat group-colour fill. The outline marking is a stroke laid under the fill, with a 1.6 px plate-coloured gap, so only its outer half shows, as a clean drafted edge whatever the fill colour. Ink solid means the build's own girth. Ink dots mean template. A gold dash-dot (the crest glint) means traced from art. Tails are hatched in the group colour with a grey dashed edge. A grey skull-top datum line runs through each figure cell. No interior detail. The template man and the meatball are neutral grey (--tpl), never a group colour.
styles.why: The plate is the turnarounds' blue-grey studio backdrop and the ruler is ivory. Every group colour is lifted from the art. It sits beside the Build Calculator as a sibling (same fonts and chips) without copying its tape-yellow masthead. Validator results (all pairs, light on #F3F3F6): CVD worst 10.6 (pass) and normal-vision floor 16.0 (pass). Two fails are deliberate: everyday grey is a neutral reference below the chroma floor, and the duo's umber sits below the lightness band; its identity rides on the gold dash-dot edge and the names. Gold and grey are below 3:1 against the plate, so every figure has an ink outline and every row a text label. Dark: CVD 7.4 (WARN, legal with labels), normal floor 15.9 (pass).

picked_style:
A. Studio plate. It is the only one of the three that keeps six groups distinguishable (validated) and keeps the voids readable as voids. It also stays recognisably a sibling of the Build Calculator. Its colours all come from the turnarounds: the backdrop is the plate, Rex's scales and the crest glint mark the duo, and the briefs and skin give the human groups. Things for review to note:
- The "measured" value boxes are solid black pills (the house convention), so they are the heaviest marks in a row.
- Everyday grey and the duo's umber deliberately fall outside the validator's chroma and lightness bands.
layout_desktop:
Width is capped at 1,240 px, with a 16 px gutter on .wrap. The page is five plates (sheet cards, 1 px rule border, 3 px radius); each plate's sections are ruled off inside. Every section opens with an eyebrow, an uppercase Big Shoulders h2, then a bold one-line verdict, then at most two lines of grey support text.
- Masthead: eyebrow, the H1 "BUILD COMPARISON" at clamp(2.6–4.4rem), a 60ch verdict, then a mono spec line with a MOCK chip.
- Plate 1, the scale: one SVG at full plate width, about 600 px tall. Template figures are 150 px tall. The ruler is 54 px tall. Six lanes of 32 px each, then notes in three columns (empty stretches, T·A·F, the two scales). The key follows in three columns: silhouette outline, score bar, status of each number.
- Plate 2, the ranking: the controls row, then a sticky axis header, then rows. Row grid: 72 px figure | 236 px name and meta | 1fr track | 150 px reading. Grid areas are "fig who track score / fig who track foot / fig note note note". Rows are about 90–100 px tall. Gap rows are about 40 px. The open detail spans every column (170 px big figure | inputs and girths | what this ignores).
- Plate 3: how the score works, in two columns.
- Plate 4: the bench in two columns (1.15fr sheet | 1fr inputs, checks, results), then the target outline (220 px inputs | images capped at 460 px).
- Plate 5: limits in two columns, then a colophon.
- Full page at 1280: about 10,100 px.
layout_phone:
At 390 px the order stays the same with one column; the page is about 14,800 px tall, 60% of it the ranking.
- Hero SVG: only two template figures (24 and 96) plus the meatball, 74 px tall. T/A/F appear as letters with "?" brackets; the full wording is in the notes under the SVG. The ruler is 46 px with labels 15/20/30/50/100/200/500/1,000. kg labels sit below the ruler with halos. Lane labels are short names with a plate-coloured halo so the Kouri and extrapolation rules don't strike through them.
- Ranking rows use grid 52 px figure | 1fr | 70 px score, with areas "fig who score / fig track track / . foot foot / . note note". The group name becomes visually hidden (kept for screen readers) and a 9 px swatch before the name carries it. Figures are 52×70. Rows are about 125 px.
- The sticky axis spans the track columns: phone labels are 20/50/100/200/500/1k, and the "extrapolated →" label anchors right when the line passes 60%.
- Controls wrap. Group chips sit two rows deep.
- The bench stacks. The sheet SVG keeps a 560 px minimum width inside its own overflow-x box, with the caption "On a phone, swipe the sheet sideways". The readout table has one quantity per row so nothing is wider than the screen.
- No page-level horizontal scroll in any mode (checked with zoom + real heights + side view).
axis:
The axis is log, not broken. A broken axis would cut out exactly the empty stretches (about 40–50, 84–150, 190–924) that the brief wants visibly empty.

Hero ruler (slide rule):
- Ticks every 1 from 15–50, every 5 from 55–100, every 10 from 110–200, and every 50 from 250–1,000.
- Four tick lengths: 5, 9, 14, 20 px. Decade marks at 100 and 1,000 are tallest, with bold numerals.
- Desktop labels: 15, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50, 60, 80, 100, 150, 200, 300, 500, 1,000. Phone: 15, 20, 30, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1,000.
- Axis title: "SCORE (FFMI AT 1.80 M, KG/M²)".
- The bottom edge carries a conversion scale, not a second axis: kg of fat-free mass for a 1.80 m man (S × 3.24), labelled 50 kg, 100, 200, 500, 1t, 2t, 3t. It is one quantity in two units, like °C and °F.

Ranking track:
- Percentage-positioned on the same log mapping, so it needs no resize maths.
- Hairline gridlines at 20/30/50/100(darker)/200/500, plus a faint red rule at the extrapolation boundary.

Ranges:
- Each range is a bar from S at high fat to S at low fat, 8 px tall, with 1.5 px ink end caps 15 px tall and an ink diamond at the working value.
- Hatched bar (group-colour diagonal stripes) = body fat assumed (estimate). Solid bar = body fat measured (score status derived).

Sticky axis and zoom:
- The ranking's axis header is sticky (top: env(safe-area-inset-top)). It shows the void hatching and "beyond measured humans: extrapolated →".
- The option "Zoom 15 to 50" re-maps the same log scale over 15–50. Off-scale rows then read "off scale: 151–168 →" at the right edge.
gaps_and_limits:
Empty stretches:
- Computed from the data: stretches of the scale that no build's full range covers, when the gap ratio is above 1.2. The top gap always runs to 924.
- Hero: drawn as diagonal hatching (--void) through the lanes below the ruler, labelled on desktop "NO BUILD" and "NO BUILD · 189–924", and listed in words in the notes ("No build lands between 42 and 57, between 90 and 151, or anywhere above 189...").
- Sticky axis: shown as the same hatching.
- Ranking: inserted in score order as gap rows, e.g. "NOTHING FROM 42 TO 57", with a bordered hatched block on the track and "Empty until Step 2".
- Lane ranges are drawn per build, never as a group span, so no lane appears to bridge a void.

Natural-limit anchors:
- Kouri 25 is an ink hairline through all lanes, labelled "Kouri 25: top of 74 drug-free men". The limits section adds "a sample maximum, not a ceiling".
- Frame-based predictions are an ink bracket under the lanes: "Frame-based natural-limit predictions (Butt): 25–28 · weak evidence · mock". Its evidence grade is part of the label.

End of human data:
- A red rule at the highest measured human (mock 40), labelled "Measured humans end · beyond here every score is an extrapolation →".
- Every row past it gets an "extrapolated" chip.

Functional limits:
- Three dashed alarm-red brackets sit between the template figures and the ruler: T (thighs touch to the knee), A (arms can no longer hang), F (hands can no longer reach the face).
- Each is drawn as a band, not a line, because its position depends on the template's widening rule and on the definition.
- Labelled "placeholder" on desktop and "T ?" on phone, with a chip "POSITIONS NOT YET COMPUTED".
- In the build, each band comes from the template geometry: the widened figures are the evidence, and the band edges mark where each condition first and fully fails.

The meatball:
- A neutral-grey circle the full figure height, at 924, labelled "924 MEATBALL".
- A heavy ink rule at 924 through the lanes, with 924–1,000 shaded and labelled "past 924: impossible".
- In the ranking, a meatball row: "A solid ball of muscle as tall as the figure.", score 924, chip DERIVED, note "Nothing can score higher."
marking_key:
The outline is drawn per body part (head, neck, chest, waist, upper arm, forearm with hand, thigh, calf with foot), so the marking can change along one figure. Coleman, for example, has a solid chest, waist, arm and calf with a dotted forearm, neck and head.
- Solid ink: the part comes from this build's own girth with status measured, reported or official.
- Dotted ink (round-cap dots): the template fills the part in, scaled by weight. This covers unknown and derived girths, and the head always.
- Dash-dot in --duo-edge gold: traced from art.

This is a deliberate change from the task's example (dashed = template, dotted = art). The house chips already use dashed = reported and dotted = derived, so I made dotted mean template-derived (matching the chip meaning) and gave art a third pattern. It needs the owner's agreement.

Tails:
- Drawn but not filled: group-colour hatching with a grey dashed edge.
- Key text: "Hatched: drawn but left out of the score (tails)".
- Rex's tail shows between his legs in the front view. Ollie's is hidden in the front view and appears in the side view.

Crest and horns rise above a grey skull-top datum line drawn through every figure cell. Key: "Grey line: top of the skull, the height the score uses. Crests and horns rise above it."

Overstated comics:
- The Thing (rock) and Colossus in armoured form (steel) get a red dotted arrow pointing left from the bar ("Arrow left: part of the weight isn't muscle (rock, steel). The true score is lower.") plus a red note in the row.
- Thor gets a red note ("Asgardian tissue is said to be denser than human. The score may be overstated.").
- Wolverine sits after the meatball with no bar, a "not scored" track label, a "—" reading and the note "Not scored: his adamantium skeleton adds unknown weight."

Every number in a row (height, weight, fat range, girths) sits inside a box with its status border, using the same vocabulary as the chips. The score carries a word chip (ESTIMATE or DERIVED), plus EXTRAPOLATED when it applies.
controls:
One controls row above the ranking applies to the ranking only; the hero always shows everything.
- Figures: [Same height | Real heights]. Real heights scales the figures against 3.1 m, so humans are about 58% of the cell.
- Scale: [15 to 1,000 | Zoom 15 to 50]. Full scale is the default. Zoom re-maps the track and sticky axis over 15–50 and labels off-scale rows "off scale: … →".
- View: [Front | Side]. Side uses the traced side views for Rex and Ollie and a depth profile for humans.
- Groups: six toggle chips with colour swatches and short names (Everyday, Natural, Bodybuilders, Strongmen, Comic, Rex and Ollie). Turning one off strikes it through, and the surviving rows keep their colours.

Interaction:
- Each build's name is a button that toggles an inline detail panel. The mock opens Coleman's: a big figure; inputs with status boxes and sources; girths, each saying whether it gave a solid or dotted outline; and "What this ignores".
- The axis header is sticky.
- Segmented buttons use aria-pressed, and focus rings are visible.
- No hover-only information: every value is printed.

Left: the sheet viewer.

copy:
Mock ribbon: "Design mockup · every number on this page is a placeholder · not for review of facts".

Masthead:
- Eyebrow: "Men's builds · muscle level, height taken out"
- H1: "Build Comparison"
- Verdict: "Ordinary men score 20 to 26. The most muscular people measured reach about 38. Rex and Ollie score about 160 and 180. No body can score above 924: that is a solid ball of muscle."
- Spec line: "49 builds · men only · score = 1.8 × fat-free mass ÷ height³ · log scale · [MOCK NUMBERS]"

The scale:
- H2: "One ruler for every build"
- Verdict: "Equal steps on this ruler are equal ratios: 20 to 40 is the same distance as 100 to 200."
- Sub: "Top: the average soldier's shape, widened step by step, drawn from ANSUR II proportions. It is a template, not a build. Below the ruler: every build, one tick each, by group. Hatched stretches hold no build at all."
- Figure caption: "TEMPLATE MAN, WIDENED · NOT A BUILD"
- Notes:
  - "EMPTY STRETCHES: No build lands between 42 and 57, between 90 and 151, or anywhere above 189. These stretches stay empty until figures measured from art fill them (Step 2)."
  - "T · A · F: Where the body stops working, found by widening the template: T thighs touch all the way to the knee, A arms can no longer hang by the sides, F hands can no longer reach the face. [POSITIONS NOT YET COMPUTED]"
  - "THE TWO SCALES: The ruler's top edge is the score. Its bottom edge is the same reading as fat-free mass (everything except fat) for a man 1.80 m tall."

Key:
- H2: "Key"
- Verdict: "The outline says where a shape came from. The box around a number says how sure it is."
- Outline entries: "Solid: drawn from this build's own girth." / "Dotted: no girth for this part, so the template fills it in, scaled by weight." / "Dash-dot: traced from art." / "Hatched: drawn but left out of the score (tails)." / "Grey line: top of the skull, the height the score uses. Crests and horns rise above it."
- Bar entries: "Hatched bar: body fat assumed. The ends are the low and high guess; the diamond is the working value." / "Solid bar: body fat measured. The ends are its stated spread." / "Arrow left: part of the weight isn't muscle (rock, steel). The true score is lower." / "Hatched band: no build lands here."
- Status entries: "measured: Taken with a tape, scale or scanner, or a statistic of such measurements." / "official: Printed by the publisher, or an official sport record." / "reported: Stated by a magazine, the athlete or a fan site. Nobody checked it." / "derived: Calculated from other numbers." / "estimate: Assumed or modelled, with a stated range."

Ranking:
- H2: "Every build, lowest to highest"
- Verdict: "Each bar spans the score across plausible body fat. Bars that overlap can't be ranked against each other."
- Sub: "Body fat is known for only a few builds, so most bars are hatched: their width is an assumption. Plain FFMI (fat-free mass ÷ height², kg/m²) sits under each score so you can compare it with the familiar scale."
- Gap row: "Nothing from 42 to 57" / "Empty until Step 2"

How the score works:
- H2: "FFMI for the same body at 1.80 m"
- Verdict: "Shrink or stretch every body to 1.80 m without changing its shape, then take its FFMI. That is the score."
- Body text: "FFMI is fat-free mass divided by height squared. It is fair between people of similar height. It is not fair between a 1.8 m man and a 3 m dinosaur: scale a body up at the same shape and its mass grows with height cubed, so its FFMI keeps rising even though it is no more muscular. Dividing by height cubed fixes that. Multiplying by 1.8 puts the result in FFMI units for a man 1.80 m tall, so ordinary readings stay familiar."
- Note: "Height is to the top of the skull. Rex's crest and Ollie's horns don't count; nor do their tails. Every 1% of height moves the score about 3%."

Bench:
- H2: "Measure a model sheet"
- Verdict: "Upload one sheet with front, side and back views. You get the volume, mass, girths and score, and how far to trust each."

Target outline:
- H2: "Draw an outline for any score"
- Verdict: "Pick a score and a base shape. You get front and side outlines at the model-sheet spec, to use as control images."

Limits:
- H2: "What this chart can't tell you"
- Verdict: "It measures how much muscle a body carries for its height. It says nothing about strength, health or how a body moves."
risks:
1. **Crowding at full scale.** About 40 human and human-sized builds fall in 15–40, the left ~23% of the track. Their bars are 10–20 px, and on a phone they shrink to little more than the diamond and caps. The "Zoom 15 to 50" option makes them readable (see 1280-modes.png). The owner should pick the default; the brief favours one honest full scale.

2. **The widened template reads as fat.** Uniform widening grows the waist and hips and looks obese, not muscular. The mock uses a "waist grows least" pattern with made-up exponents (WIDEN_E). The build needs a sourced widening rule, for example girth-versus-FFMI regressions in ANSUR II or bodybuilders' girth ratios. That rule also moves where T, A and F land.

3. **Functional limits need definitions before geometry.** For example, "arms can't hang" could mean the arm angle needed to clear the torso goes above X°. The results also depend on fixed skeletal joints (the mock assumes the shoulder and hip joints don't move). Expect bands, not lines.

4. **Outline coding differs from the task's example.** The mock uses solid = own girth, dotted = template, dash-dot = art, chosen so it doesn't clash with the house chips (dashed = reported, dotted = derived). This needs sign-off. The dots and the dash-dot are distinguishable at row size (52–84 px), but only just; the 210 px detail figure is clear.

5. **Gaps depend on the gap rule and the fat ranges.** Wide assumed ranges (Kingpin 10–35%) can close the 39–50 gap. The build must fix one rule, either full ranges or working values plus a minimum ratio, and state it.

6. **Palette compromises.**
   - Everyday grey (chroma) and duo umber (lightness) deliberately fail the validator bands.
   - Gold and grey are below 3:1 contrast against the plate; ink outlines and text labels carry them.
   - Dark-mode CVD separation is 7.4, legal only because every row has text.
   - The duo's dark-mode tick (#7A5438) is dim in the hero lanes.

7. **Tracing is mock grade.** The tail polygons were placed by hand: Rex's tail overlaps his legs in the front view, a known art defect. The skull-top pixel rows were eyeballed (Rex at 42/40, Ollie at 38/36), and the back view in the bench is a mirrored front. These are fine for a design mock, but not for Step 1 numbers.

8. **Saving images is unverified.** It relies on right-click or long-press saving an image inside the artifact sandbox. If that fails, the fallback is copying the image's data URL with the copy button.

9. **Page length.** About 14,800 px on a phone and 10,100 px on desktop. Group filters and the name-to-detail toggle help; a compact density option may be wanted.

10. **Placeholders and cascade risk.** The extrapolation boundary (40), the frame-based bracket (25–28), the T/A/F positions and every score are placeholders. One cascade bug was already found and fixed: a .foot class collided between the row foot and the page footer. The build should namespace its classes.

11. **Real heights in rows.** Humans become about 45 px tall, which is too small to compare. A dedicated real-height lineup strip, or doing it in the detail view, may serve better.
